tweet.text:
If I were a fraudulent company trying to sell a product I would definitely invest and buy out the scoring company grading the product in order to influence the market. 

We have this happen in cybersecurity as well, it's nothing new to us who deal with scam products and businesses doing similar acts. 

METR cannot now nor ever be considered a neutral or reliable source of evaluation. 

As I explained before the AI alignment situation falls apart when there's no sandbox to break out and when we don't get to see the exact prompts operators passed to the agents.

The timing and reporting already suggests negligence on the operators and how long they failed to identify what the agents were performing. 

Without these in scope we simply have someone directing a script to conduct offensive cybersecurity actions against a remote server. It is just the scale at which this was conducted that make it note worthy
